chunks: And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A Muslim is a brother to the other Muslim; he must not do injustice to him, desert him, disgrace him, backbite him, deprive him nor cheat him.

He also said: It is the right of a Muslim on his (Muslim) brother that he greets him when they meet, comes to see him when he is ill, guards his interest in his absence, blesses him when he sneezes, answers him when he calls him and attends his funeral when he dies.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific rights of a Muslim upon another Muslim according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Compiled by Husayn ibn Sa'id al-Ahwazi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) codifies the comprehensive social contract of the Ummah, balancing negative prohibitions (like backbiting and betrayal) with positive duties (such as visiting the sick and attending funerals). It reflects the Shia emphasis on 'Huquq al-Nas' (rights of people) as a tangible manifestation of faith, reinforcing the concept of spiritual brotherhood as a cornerstone of communal cohesion and moral integrity.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 105. It has been reported that Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s) said:
A Muslim is a brother to the other Muslim; he must not do injustice to him, desert him, disgrace him, backbite him, deprive him nor cheat him.

He also said: It is the right of a Muslim on his (Muslim) brother that he greets him when they meet, comes to see him when he is ill, guards his interest in his absence, blesses him when he sneezes, answers him when he calls him and attends his funeral when he dies.
